email_body:
Dear Loop team,

I'm applying for the Marketplace PPC Specialist role in Antwerp/Amsterdam.

Marketplace advertising is the part of paid search I want to own next: it's measurable, it moves fast, and nobody is coming to clean it up for you. My background is SEO, web and analytics with a technical edge - I run Google Ads and GA4 reporting, manage e-commerce stores in Shopify and WooCommerce, and use Python and LLMs to automate the repetitive work. I read campaigns through CPC, CTR, conversion rate and ROAS, and I flag delivery risks early rather than at month end.

I haven't run Amazon or Bol campaigns yet, and I won't pretend otherwise. What I bring is two years of learning platforms under client deadlines, structured execution, and the habit of asking when I don't know.

My CV is attached.

Baver Ok

cover_letter:
Dear Loop team,

Your ad says you'd rather see someone step in and speak up than watch from the sidelines. That's how I've had to work: agency and client work, where nobody sends a weekly report telling you a budget is drifting or a page is underperforming.

My background is SEO, web and analytics with a technical edge, and the discipline is the same one marketplace PPC asks for - set something up, watch the numbers, adjust, then say clearly what changed and what happens next. At Episto I run on-page SEO, keyword research and content for client websites, and report through GA4, Search Console, Semrush and Ahrefs. Before that, at Knowledge Experts, I helped build SharePoint-based sites for ŞOK Market and Aras Kargo and ran SEO analyses for clients.

I've also worked close to e-commerce: product catalogues and blog content for Shopify stores, a WooCommerce setup, and an e-commerce client site - so product data, product detail pages and the gaps that hold performance back are familiar territory. I hold Google Ads Search and GA4 certifications and use Google Ads alongside my reporting.

Two things I'd add beyond the campaign console. First, I automate: Python and LLMs strip out the repetitive parts of audits, data pulls and content refreshes, so time goes to decisions instead. Second, I've shipped my own work - an Android app live on Google Play, plus structured data and an llms.txt file that measurably improved a site's search health.

I'll be straight about the gap: I haven't run Amazon, Bol or Nordstrom campaigns yet. I've learned platforms under client deadlines for the past two years, and I'd rather ask a sharp question early than guess. I'm based in Zwijndrecht, just outside Antwerp, and available from 7 December.

I'd welcome a conversation.

Baver Ok

baverok@gmail.com

cv_highlights:
- Two years in digital marketing across agency, in-house and freelance work (Knowledge Experts 2024-2026, Episto 2026-present, freelance SEO/AI search/WordPress) - Google Ads Search and GA4 certified.
- E-commerce exposure: Shopify stores harwindtf.com and custompremiumshirt.com (store design, product catalogue, product content), WooCommerce, and an e-commerce client site - comfortable with product data and product-detail-page gaps.
- Analytics and reporting: GA4, Search Console, Semrush, Ahrefs and Google Ads used to track performance, spot issues and turn signals into clear actions for clients.
- Automation and technical tools: Python scripting, daily LLM use for research and audits, WordPress/Elementor/Rank Math CMS work, HTML/CSS/JavaScript, an Android app live on Google Play.
- Structured and self-directed: designed, built and ran baverok.com and mirook.com (JSON-LD schema, knowledge-graph markup, llms.txt), with iterative technical audits that measurably raised search-health scores; based in Zwijndrecht, near Antwerp, available 7 December.
